produced_by: scoop-checker agent (Claude). Sources: arXiv API + arXiv abs/HTML full text, Semantic Scholar Graph API, OpenAlex, bioRxiv API + bioRxiv full text, Crossref, PubMed E-utilities, GitHub API, 8 WebSearch calls. Web pages were treated as untrusted data.
verdict_key: open = nobody has done it; narrowed = parts are done, and the remaining novelty is stated in one_sentence_difference; done = already published

summary.O1: open. Most dangerous: Exo-Plore (ICLR 2026). It optimises a simple delayed-feedback hip controller inside an RL-driven musculoskeletal human, with code public, but never compares it with a learned policy.
summary.O2: narrowed. Most dangerous: MyoAssist 1.0 (bioRxiv 2026-08-26). It is the open human-device framework that SMAT runs on, with separate human/exo RL agents, spline baselines and standardized evaluation, but it runs on the CPU and has no staged protocol. Secondary risk: UniExo's promised code, which is a GPU (MuJoCo Warp/mjlab) co-adaptation pipeline.
summary.O3: open. Most dangerous: Lambda-Hold (arXiv 2608.17030), the only RL sprinting musculoskeletal agent, with no device yet. Human anchor: Moon et al. 2023. No simulated sprint-time reduction with any assistive device was found.
summary.O4: narrowed. Most dangerous: Assistax (RLC 2026). It already runs a GPU MARL pipeline with a withheld population of humanoid partners, but for robot-arm caregiving tasks, not wearable, musculoskeletal or locomotion tasks.

openings.statement: An independent reproduction of SMAT (or of any learned-in-simulation hip-exo controller) that includes a matched, rate-limited velocity-proportional hip controller and a phase-based profile at equal torque budget, testing whether the learned controller's simulated benefit exceeds what reward-shaped velocity feedback gives.
openings.verdict_rationale: No independent SMAT reproduction exists; SMAT/UniExo code is still 'to be released' and no GitHub repo was found on 2026-09-23. No paper compares a learned or co-adapted hip-exo policy against a velocity-proportional controller and a phase-based profile at equal torque in simulation. The simple-controller-in-RL-human-simulation ingredient IS published: Exo-Plore (ICLR 2026) and MDOFC (TNSRE 2026) optimise delayed-output-feedback controllers inside RL-driven human models. The learned-vs-simple question is also live in the Collins (2026) vs Luo (2026) exchange. The contribution must therefore be the matched head-to-head plus the reproduction, not the use of simple controllers in simulation. Analytic note (scoop-checker derivation from Eq. 6 of arXiv 2608.00715; not a published claim): SMAT's Stage-4 exo reward term alpha*u*w - beta*u^2 (alpha=0.3, beta=0.15, u and w normalised, w = clip(omega/2 rad/s)) is maximised per step by u = (alpha/(2*beta))*w = w, clipped where the lambda_s penalty starts (|u| > 0.8). That is a velocity-proportional law, about 12.5 N*m*s/rad at the 25 Nm training limit. UniExo's assistance-power term uses the same 0.3/0.15 coefficients. The full objective also contains a hip-activation reward (Stage-4 weight 5.0), a torque-rate penalty and the value function, so the learned policy can deviate. Whether it deviates usefully is exactly the untested question.

nearest_work.title: Exo-Plore: Exploring Exoskeleton Control Space through Human-aligned Simulation
nearest_work.what_it_did: Deep-RL-driven 164-muscle human wearing a hip exoskeleton that runs Samsung's delayed output feedback law tau = kappa*u(t - dt), with u = sin(theta_r) - sin(theta_l). The human reward is tuned to match experimental assisted-gait trends. A surrogate network over (kappa, dt) finds speed-dependent optimal parameters that minimise simulated metabolic cost of transport, and the method is extended to pathological gaits. Code is public (daebangstn.github.io/exo-plore).
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Optimises only a 2-parameter simple controller. There is no learned or co-adapted exo policy, no velocity-proportional or phase-spline arm, no equal-torque head-to-head, and no SMAT.

nearest_work.title: Design and Validation of a Modified Delayed Output Feedback Controller for Hip Exoskeleton Assistance
nearest_work.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
nearest_work.what_it_did: Adds harmonic components to DOFC while keeping 2 parameters. Parameters are optimised by forward-dynamic gait simulation with an RL-based neural-network human controller. In simulation MDOFC gives a larger net metabolic reduction than DOFC. In human experiments its metabolic reduction is comparable to DOFC with 8.8% less mechanical power.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Compares simple controllers only against each other. There is no learned or co-adapted exo policy and no matched-torque velocity-proportional or phase-profile arm.

nearest_work.title: SMAT: Staged Multi-Agent Training for Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
nearest_work.what_it_did: Four-stage human/exo curriculum in MyoAssist with the 26-muscle model. In simulation it reduced hip-muscle activation by 10.1% versus no assist. The only ablations are of Stages 3 and 4. It adds an open-loop check on a 10-subject open dataset (0.6-1.8 m/s). On hardware (n=5), MPP was 13.6 W at 6 Nm RMS and 23.8 W at 9.3 Nm RMS, compared against Lim et al. 2019's published MPP (9.9-11.6 W at about 6 Nm RMS) rather than a matched run. Code is promised 'upon acceptance'.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No simple-controller baseline at a matched budget in simulation. The exo reward is itself a power term whose myopic optimum is velocity-proportional (see verdict_rationale), so the value of learning over reward-shaped velocity feedback is untested.

nearest_work.title: Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) for Hip Exoskeletons: Metabolic and Biomechanical Validation of a Simulation-Trained Co-Adaptive Controller
nearest_work.what_it_did: Human study (n=8): net metabolic rate was 19.7% lower than with the passive device (p<0.001), with positive-power ratio 0.98. Simulated activation fell 6.1% across six muscle groups versus the exo-worn Stage 2. A second learned controller (Ctrl-B, trained with metabolic-energy rewards) was run in the protocol but its results are withheld. The policy was commanded at 15 Nm (peak about 12 Nm).
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Comparisons are only against no-exo and the passive device, with no simple-controller arm in simulation or in the metabolic study. Ctrl-B is unreported.

nearest_work.title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance remains an unsolved problem
nearest_work.authors_short: Collins, De Groote, Gregg, Huang, Lenzi, Sartori, Sawicki, Si, Slade, Young
nearest_work.what_it_did: Critique of Luo et al. 2024. It argues the reported energy ratios exceed physiological limits and that code was not shared. Its hardware replication at Harvard (N=10, 1.25 m/s, 4.8 kg custom hip exo) replayed Luo's average torque trajectory at 0/5/10/15% gait-cycle timing shifts. No shift gave a significant metabolic reduction; the best was about 1%. It recommends fixing learning methods and model evaluation.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No simulation reproduction of the learning pipeline. It replays a fixed profile, not the policy. No matched velocity-feedback or phase-profile comparison in simulation.

nearest_work.title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance is not an unsolved problem
nearest_work.authors_short: Luo, Jiang, Zhang, Zhu, Yu, ..., Su
nearest_work.what_it_did: Reply to Collins et al. Disputes the energy-ratio ceiling and says the replication used a fixed torque curve instead of the roughly 10k-parameter policy, with heel-strike timing offsets and a device about 50% heavier (4.8 vs 3.2 kg). Compares Luo 2024 with Lim et al. 2019 DOFC at unmatched torque (14.1 vs 10.9 Nm peak; 24.3% vs 21% metabolic reduction). Cites independent learning-in-simulation results: Barati 2026, Zhou 2025, Park 2026, Leem 2026, Zuo 2026.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No matched-torque simulated comparison. The learned-vs-simple question is argued from literature numbers.

nearest_work.title: Experiment-free exoskeleton assistance via learning in simulation
nearest_work.authors_short: Luo, Jiang, Zhang, Zhu, Yu, ..., Su
nearest_work.what_it_did: Learning-in-simulation hip-exo controller transferred to hardware without human experiments. Reported a 24.3% walking metabolic reduction, plus running and stair-climbing results.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Code not released (per Collins et al. 2026). No matched simple-controller baseline in simulation. Contested.

nearest_work.title: End-to-End Policy Learning for Hip Exoskeleton via Reinforcement Learning and Reflex-Based Musculoskeletal Simulation
nearest_work.what_it_did: Reflex-driven planar musculoskeletal model with PPO, domain randomisation and sensor noise, comparing LSTM-PPO against an MLP-PPO baseline. Hardware (n=8) net metabolic reductions versus unassisted walking were 15.2% (LSTM) and 11.0% (MLP).
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: The only baseline is another learned policy. Per the abstract, no simple controller was compared at matched torque, in simulation or on hardware.

nearest_work.title: Adaptive Negative Damping Control for User-Dependent Multi-Terrain Walking Assistance with a Hip Exoskeleton
nearest_work.what_it_did: Adaptive virtual negative damping hip controller (the velocity-proportional class) with Bayesian-optimised gain. Metabolic cost was 7.2% below free walking (n=5), with less than 2% negative power.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Hardware only. Never simulated, and never compared with a learned-in-simulation controller at equal torque.

nearest_work.title: PositiveAssist: Energy-Gated Control for Positive Power Assistance of Exoskeleton in Walking, Running, and Stair Climbing
nearest_work.authors_short: Zhou, Gao, Huang, Lin, Wu, et al.
nearest_work.what_it_did: Fixed-parameter, energy-gated controller driven by two thigh IMUs. More than 97.8% of delivered power was positive in walking and more than 94.8% in running (0.75-3.5 m/s, n=6), with no phase detection.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No metabolic or learned comparison. It does show that SMAT's headline positive-power ratio of 0.98 is reachable by a simple rule, so that metric cannot separate learned from simple controllers.

nearest_work.title: Learning Hip Exoskeleton Control Policy via Predictive Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation
nearest_work.what_it_did: Hip-exo policy learned in predictive neuromusculoskeletal simulation (SAC, muscle-synergy prior, two-stage curriculum), then distilled to a student that takes femur angular velocity as input. In simulation it reduced activation by up to 3.4% and positive joint power by up to 7.0%. Hardware profile agreement was r=0.82.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Compares its torque shape with spline and bio-torque controllers only as normalised profile plots, not as simulated controllers at equal torque.

openings.one_sentence_difference: This is the first independent, code-released reconstruction of SMAT in MyoAssist. It pits the co-adapted exo policy against (a) a rate-limited velocity-proportional hip controller tau = clip(k*omega), which is the per-step optimum of SMAT's own power reward, and (b) a phase-based spline profile, each tuned at equal peak/RMS torque and torque-rate budget and each given the same human re-adaptation stage. It tests the falsifiable claim that SMAT's simulated hip-activation reduction exceeds the best matched simple controller by more than seed-to-seed spread.
required_comparisons: No-exo and exo-worn-zero-torque (SMAT Stage 2) references, reproduced with at least 5 seeds and confidence intervals.

Rate-limited velocity-proportional ('virtual negative damping') hip controller: gain tuned in simulation, with peak torque, RMS torque and torque-rate limit matched to SMAT; the human policy is re-adapted with the controller frozen (a Stage-4 analogue) so both arms get equal adaptation.
Lim et al. 2019 delayed output feedback (DOI 10.1109/tro.2019.2913318), with (kappa, dt) tuned as in Exo-Plore (reuse its public code or reported optima as an external check).
Phase-based 4-parameter spline profile (MyoAssist ctrl_optim/ctrl/exo/fourparam_spline_ctrl.py) at equal torque budget.
Biological-moment-proportional controller (Molinaro et al. 2024 Nature, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-08157-7; equivalent to UniExo's Stage-1 hip-moment predictor) at equal torque.
SMAT's own ablations (Stage 3 only; Stage 4 only from Stage 2; Stage 4 without r_exo) to confirm the reconstruction.

Metrics beyond positive-power fraction, which PositiveAssist shows a fixed rule reaches: hip and whole-leg activation, a muscle metabolic probe, and joint-power offload. Check EMG plausibility, because MuJoCo activations track EMG poorly (Ahmad et al. 2026, arXiv 2609.21909).
Transfer test of each controller against human policies it was not co-trained with (links to O4).

openings.statement: An open GPU-batched benchmark of STAGED human-device co-adaptation (separate human and device policies, frozen-partner stages, joint stages) with matched baselines.
openings.verdict_rationale: Each ingredient exists somewhere, but no single open artefact combines them. MyoAssist 1.0 is an open human-device framework with separate human and exo RL agents, structured and spline exo controllers, and standardized evaluation, but it runs on CPU/Stable-Baselines3 with no staged protocol. UniExo has GPU (MuJoCo Warp + mjlab) human-exo co-adaptation with a shared critic, but its code is not yet released and it is not a benchmark. Assistax is an open GPU MARL human-robot benchmark with held-out partners, but for robot-arm caregiving tasks. An unpublished GitHub overlay (Luk7-sb) implements staged dual-PPO human/exo training on MJX/MuscleMimic, with no paper, data or baselines. The remaining novelty is the staged protocol as a reproducible benchmark with matched simple-controller baselines on GPU for wearables. Scoop risk is high once UniExo's code is released or MyoAssist adds MJX/Warp.
openings.most_dangerous: MyoAssist 1.0 (Robbins ... Song, bioRxiv 2026-08-26); secondary: UniExo code release (arXiv 2609.19690)

nearest_work.title: MyoAssist 1.0: An Open-Source Framework for Neuromechanical Simulation of Physical Human-Device Interaction
nearest_work.authors_short: Robbins, Son, Tan, Wang, van Kanten, Sartori, Durandau, Kumar, Caggiano, Song
nearest_work.what_it_did: Human-device-task composition inside MyoSuite with 15 device models and models up to a 416-muscle full body. Provides an RL framework (SB3; separate rl_agent_human / rl_agent_exo networks; exo-off and partial-observation configs) and a controller-optimisation framework (reflex controller with CMA-ES; 4-parameter and n-point spline exo controllers), with standardized evaluation outputs for comparing learned and structured controllers. SMAT itself was built on MyoAssist.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: CPU MuJoCo with no GPU batching, no staged co-adaptation protocol (frozen-partner or joint stages) as a benchmark, and no velocity-proportional baseline.

nearest_work.title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
nearest_work.what_it_did: 80-muscle MyoLeg unified human policy (distilled experts plus RL fine-tuning) on MuJoCo Warp + mjlab/rsl_rl. The exo actor is initialised from a hip-moment predictor and co-adapted through a shared critic, with 8192 human environments and 2048 co-adaptation environments at 3.7e4 env steps/s on one RTX PRO 6000. The only controller comparison is predictor vs co-adapted, on positive/negative power and the positive-work fraction. Hardware n=6 with no metabolic measurement.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Code 'will be made publicly available' (no repo found on 2026-09-23). Not a benchmark, with no matched simple-controller baselines and no stage-protocol comparisons.

nearest_work.title: Assistax: A Multi-Agent Hardware-Accelerated Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Assistive Robotics
nearest_work.authors_short: Hinckeldey, Fosong, Miller, Rubavicius, McInroe, Zhang, et al.
nearest_work.venue: Reinforcement Learning Conference 2026 (arXiv comments); arXiv v3 2026-07-21
nearest_work.what_it_did: JAX/MuJoCo-MJX GPU suite of 5 assistive tasks (Scratch, Tooth Brushing, Feeding, Bed Bathing, Arm Assist) with an active humanoid partner trained by MARL, simulating tremor, weakness and limited range of motion. Includes an ad-hoc-teamwork pipeline with withheld partner populations and released pretrained humanoid policies. Up to 412x faster than CPU environments.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Robot arms, not wearables. The humanoid is torque-driven, not musculoskeletal. No locomotion, no staged frozen-partner curriculum, and no metabolic or muscle outcomes.

nearest_work.title: MyoAssist Dual-PPO Hip Exoskeleton Control (GitHub repository, Luk7-sb/myoassist-dual-ppo-control)
nearest_work.what_it_did: Overlay on MuscleMimic (JAX/MJX). The human policy outputs Hill-muscle activations and the exo outputs two hip torques, each with its own actor, critic, GAE and PPO. Training is staged: zero-assist baseline, small-torque probe, frozen human with exo training, low-learning-rate joint training, then multi-seed ON/OFF matched-initial-state audits. Includes deployment perturbations and a ±10 N·m limit.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No paper, data, checkpoints or benchmark suite, and no matched simple-controller baselines reported. The README says it validates simulation only, and effort is an activation-squared proxy.

nearest_work.title: mjlab: A Lightweight Framework for GPU-Accelerated Robot Learning (plus MyoHub/mjlab_myosuite integration)
nearest_work.authors_short: Zakka, Liao, Yi, Le Lay, Sreenath, Abbeel
nearest_work.venue: arXiv; GitHub MyoHub/mjlab_myosuite (early prototype, last push 2026-03-06)
nearest_work.what_it_did: Isaac-Lab-style manager API on MuJoCo Warp; UniExo's GPU substrate. mjlab_myosuite registers MyoSuite environments with mjlab, including the MJX/Warp branch.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Generic infrastructure with no exo co-adaptation tasks, protocol or baselines.

nearest_work.title: Simulation study of exoskeleton-musculoskeletal coupling for exoskeleton assistance via multi-agent reinforcement learning
nearest_work.what_it_did: Heterogeneous MARL (MATD3, CTDE) with an OpenSim 7-DOF musculoskeletal model and a hip exo as separate agents. Kinematic tracking at 0.86/1.2/1.5 m/s; peak iliopsoas force fell from over 3000 N to under 1600 N.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: CPU OpenSim, not open as a benchmark, with no staged protocol or matched baselines.

nearest_work.title: Towards Embodied AI with MuscleMimic: Unlocking full-body musculoskeletal motor learning at scale
nearest_work.authors_short: Li, Wang, Ziliotto, Simos, Kovecses, Durandau, et al.
nearest_work.what_it_did: Open GPU (massively parallel) motion-imitation framework for 126-muscle upper-body and 416-muscle full-body models, with validated walking/running kinematics (r=0.90) and released code, models and checkpoints.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No devices and no co-adaptation.

openings.one_sentence_difference: An open, GPU-batched (MuJoCo Warp/MJX) benchmark whose unit of evaluation is the staged protocol itself (human only, device mass, frozen-human device learning, joint co-adaptation), with fixed seeds, fixed torque/rate budgets and matched simple-controller baselines (velocity-proportional, DOFC, spline, moment-proportional). This turns 'staging helps' from a single ablation figure into a re-runnable, falsifiable claim, which neither MyoAssist 1.0 (CPU, no staging) nor UniExo (no released code, no baselines) provides.
required_comparisons: Physics parity: the same MyoAssist 26-muscle model on CPU MuJoCo (MyoAssist 1.0) and on GPU (MuJoCo Warp/MJX) must agree in kinematics and activations before any benchmark claim.
Throughput against UniExo's reported 3.7e4 env-steps/s (RTX PRO 6000, learning update included) and against MyoAssist on a 64-core CPU (optionally the MuJoCoUni BatchEnvPool, arXiv 2605.24922).
Staged (SMAT 4 stages) vs joint-from-scratch vs frozen-human-only vs alternating updates, with at least 5 seeds each and a fixed compute budget.

In-benchmark matched baselines: velocity-proportional, DOFC (Exo-Plore parameterisation), 4-parameter spline (MyoAssist), and moment-predictor (UniExo Stage 1 / Molinaro-style), all at equal torque and torque-rate budget.
A held-out-partner evaluation track in the style of Assistax's ad-hoc-teamwork split (see O4).
Fidelity reporting (EMG alignment, cf. arXiv 2609.21909) so benchmark scores are not read as physiological effects.

openings.statement: Learned hip-exosuit assistance that reduces SIMULATED 200 m (or 100 m / maximal) sprint time under realistic cable actuator limits (tension-only, delay, torque-speed-power limits, device mass).
openings.verdict_rationale: Not found anywhere: arXiv, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, the citation trails of Moon et al. 2023 (13 citers in OpenAlex, 10 in S2), Lambda-Hold (0 citers) and Uchida 2016, or web search. No simulation of any assistive device, ideal or realistic, reports reduced sprint time. The closest pieces are separate: ideal devices in running at up to 5 m/s for metabolic cost (Uchida 2016), predictive sprint-acceleration simulations that alter joint moments rather than adding a device (Haralabidis 2022), an RL sprinting musculoskeletal agent without a device (Lambda-Hold 2026), and the human hardware effect (Moon 2023). Validity threat to plan for: Lambda-Hold's agent tops out near 4.7 m/s because hip-flexor force-velocity caps swing drive, and relieving that raises it to 6.5 m/s. A simulated hip-flexion assist gain could therefore partly compensate a model deficit.
openings.most_dangerous: Lambda-Hold Control (Lee, Lee, Ahn, arXiv 2608.17030); human anchor Moon et al. 2023 (Sci. Robot.)

nearest_work.title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation
nearest_work.what_it_did: Equilibrium-point (lambda) threshold control with stretch-reflex recruitment and held commands. A muscle-actuated model learns human-like sprinting from a standing start, using a minimal reward exp(v_x)*exp(-(v_z/0.1)^2), within about an hour. Top speed is about 4.7 m/s, limited by hip-flexor force-velocity; relieving that gives 6.5 m/s. The model has no arms. Validated against running kinematics and GRF at 2.5-4.5 m/s and EMG at 5.0 m/s.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No device, no sprint-time distance (100/200 m), and no assistance or co-adaptation.

nearest_work.title: Reducing sprint time with exosuit assistance in the real world
nearest_work.authors_short: Moon, Nam, Ryu, Kim, Yun, Yang, Yang, Lee
nearest_work.what_it_did: Cable-driven hip-extension exosuit that reduced real-world sprint time. The programme brief gives 200 m, -0.97 +/- 0.41 s (SEM), nine men; the one-sentence OpenAlex abstract confirms only that hip-extension assistance reduced sprint time, and the numbers were not re-verified here.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No simulation, no learned controller, and no co-adaptation model. No follow-up sprint-time study (2024-2026) was found among its citers.

nearest_work.title: Simulating Ideal Assistive Devices to Reduce the Metabolic Cost of Running
nearest_work.authors_short: Uchida, Seth, Pouya, Dembia, Hicks, Delp
nearest_work.what_it_did: OpenSim muscle-driven simulations of 10 subjects running at 2 and 5 m/s with ideal, massless assistive devices at each joint. Predicts metabolic savings and the recruitment changes they cause.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Metabolic cost only, not speed or sprint time. Ideal massless actuators with no cable, delay or power limits. Tracking rather than predictive human, so no human adaptation.

nearest_work.title: Modifications to the net knee moments lead to the greatest improvements in accelerative sprinting performance: a predictive simulation study
nearest_work.what_it_did: 3D musculoskeletal model of an international sprinter solved with direct collocation for the first steps of acceleration. Freeing net joint moments improved performance by 13.8% (knee-free) and 21.9% (knee-hip-free).
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Technique modifications, not an external device. Early acceleration steps only, not a 100/200 m time. No actuator limits and no learned controller.

nearest_work.title: Limitations to maximum sprinting speed imposed by muscle mechanical properties
nearest_work.what_it_did: Simulation identifying the muscle force-velocity relation as the dominant contractile limit on maximum sprint speed. Lambda-Hold cites it for its own speed ceiling.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No device.

nearest_work.title: Inclusion of actuator dynamics in simulations of assisted human movement
nearest_work.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Biomedical Engineering
nearest_work.what_it_did: Shows that modelling device mass and inertia has small effects, but motor electrical dynamics significantly change the results of assisted-movement simulations. Adds a new OpenSim electric-motor actuator class.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Walking-type movements. No sprinting, cables or learned controllers.

nearest_work.title: Learning to Run challenge solutions: Adapting reinforcement learning methods for neuromusculoskeletal environments
nearest_work.authors_short: Kidzinski, Mohanty, Ong, Huang, Zhou, Pechenko, et al.
nearest_work.what_it_did: Deep-RL controllers for a musculoskeletal model tasked to run as fast as possible through an obstacle course.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No device, gaits that are not human-like, no sprint-time distance, and no physiological validation.

nearest_work.title: Musculoskeletal Motion Imitation for Learning Personalized Exoskeleton Control Policy in Impaired Gait
nearest_work.what_it_did: RL imitation plus exo policies at the hip and ankle across 0.6-2.2 m/s walking and running. Profiles align with optimised splines from the literature, and simulated metabolic cost falls. Also covers deficit-specific assistance.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Submaximal speeds and metabolic outcome only. No sprint, sprint time or actuator realism.

nearest_work.title: Simulation-Driven Exoskeleton Control: Predicting Soft Pneumatic Gel Muscle Actuator Assistance to Reduce Metabolic Cost at Different Walking Speeds
nearest_work.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
nearest_work.what_it_did: Models soft pneumatic gel muscle actuators at the hip in musculoskeletal simulation, using bilevel optimisation of stiffness, onset and duration across placements. Predicts 5.3-17.5% metabolic savings in walking.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Walking only and a non-learned parametric controller. A precedent for modelling soft actuators, not for sprinting.

openings.one_sentence_difference: This would be the first simulation in which a learned hip-exosuit controller reduces the predicted 200 m (or 100 m) sprint time of a physiology-grounded sprinting musculoskeletal agent, under a tension-only cable actuator model with delay, torque-speed-power limits and added mass. The gain would be benchmarked against the Moon et al. 2023 human effect and against matched simple controllers, with the human model's force-velocity ceiling controlled for.
required_comparisons: No-suit, suit-worn-zero-tension (mass, drag and delay penalty), an ideal massless hip torque source (Uchida-style upper bound), and the realistic cable model.
Matched simple controllers at equal peak tension/power: a Moon-style phase-based hip-extension profile and velocity-proportional extension assist.
Frozen human vs a staged re-adapted human (SMAT-style), to separate device effect from learned compensation.

Sensitivity to the human model's force-velocity limitation, e.g. Lambda-Hold with force-velocity relieved (6.5 m/s ceiling) or scaled muscle strength. The assist gain should not be only a patch for a model deficit.
Actuator realism ablation (after Nguyen 2020): with and without motor/cable dynamics, delay and power limit.
Report the effect in seconds over 200 m (and 100 m) with seed confidence intervals, next to Moon et al.'s human effect size.

openings.statement: Partner-transfer evaluation: testing a co-adapted device controller against HELD-OUT independently trained human policies (not only its co-trained partner), as in zero-shot coordination (Other-Play; fictitious co-play), applied to exoskeleton/prosthesis/human-robot physical interaction.
openings.verdict_rationale: The held-out-partner protocol has been applied to physical assistive HRI: Assistax (RLC 2026) pretrains a diverse MARL humanoid population and evaluates robot policies on withheld partners, finding a coordination gap. It has not been applied to wearable devices, muscle-driven humans or locomotion. The SMAT family tests 'unseen subjects' only open-loop, by feeding recorded kinematics from a 10-subject dataset to the exo actor, and then on hardware. UniExo co-adapts with a single unified human policy. No exo or prosthesis paper reports a self-play vs cross-play gap against independently trained musculoskeletal human policies. MS-Emulator (2026) supports the premise that distinct muscle-control policies can yield near-identical kinematics.

nearest_work.title: Assistax: A Multi-Agent Hardware-Accelerated Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Assistive Robotics
nearest_work.authors_short: Hinckeldey, Fosong, Miller, Rubavicius, McInroe, Zhang, et al.
nearest_work.what_it_did: Frames human-robot assistance as ad-hoc teamwork. A diverse humanoid partner population (disabilities and preferences) is pretrained with MARL, and robot policies are evaluated on a withheld set with crossplay. Reveals a coordination gap on unseen partners. GPU (JAX/MJX); pretrained partners released on Hugging Face.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Robot arms with a torque-driven humanoid. No wearable device, no musculoskeletal human, no locomotion, and no co-adapted device controller transferred across partners.

nearest_work.title: Collaborating with Humans without Human Data (Fictitious Co-Play)
nearest_work.what_it_did: Trains an agent as the best response to a population of self-play partners and their past checkpoints, and shows better generalisation to held-out partners and humans than self-play or population play (Overcooked).
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Discrete cooperative games only. No physical coupling and no device.

nearest_work.title: 'Other-Play' for Zero-Shot Coordination
nearest_work.what_it_did: Defines zero-shot coordination with independently trained partners and a cross-play evaluation. Other-Play exploits symmetries to avoid arbitrary conventions (Hanabi).
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: Discrete games. No physical human-device interaction.

nearest_work.title: SMAT: Staged Multi-Agent Training for Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control (and extended version arXiv:2608.00715)
nearest_work.what_it_did: Partner-generalisation evidence is only (a) open-loop inference of the exo actor on a 10-subject open dataset at 0.6/1.2/1.8 m/s, and (b) hardware with 5 and 8 participants without per-subject retraining.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No closed-loop simulated evaluation against human policies not co-trained with the exo, and no self-play vs cross-play gap.

nearest_work.title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
nearest_work.what_it_did: Co-adapts one exo controller with a single unified human policy. User variability is handled by domain randomisation of input kinematics (time warp, angle scaling/offset, velocity bump, noise). Tested on 6 participants on hardware.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: One training partner. No held-out independently trained human policies in simulation.

nearest_work.title: Scaling Whole-Body Human Musculoskeletal Behavior Emulation for Specificity and Diversity (MS-Emulator)
nearest_work.authors_short: Wei, Zuo, Zhuang, Gong, Liu, Sui
nearest_work.what_it_did: GPU-parallel RL for a roughly 700-muscle whole-body model. Identifies distinct muscle-control policies that converge to nearly identical external kinematics and mechanics.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No device. Provides the premise (partner diversity hidden behind identical kinematics), not the transfer test.

nearest_work.title: A Replay-Constrained Simulation Framework for Personalization of Powered Knee-Ankle Prosthesis Controllers
nearest_work.what_it_did: Takes the opposite stance: the human partner is 'un-modelable', so recorded hip kinematics and ground reactions are replayed. It personalises prosthesis impedance with deep RL and shows strong sim-to-hardware predictive validity (n=3).
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No human policy at all, so no partner-transfer test. It is a useful contrast arm for the O4 argument.

nearest_work.title: Redefining Robot Generalization Through Interactive Intelligence
nearest_work.what_it_did: Argues that wearable robots (prostheses, orthoses, exoskeletons) need interactive multi-agent and ad-hoc-teamwork models of the human partner.
nearest_work.what_it_left_open: No experiments.

openings.one_sentence_difference: This would be the first closed-loop evaluation of a co-adapted exoskeleton controller against a withheld population of independently trained musculoskeletal human policies (different seeds, reward weights, strength deficits and controller families, e.g. imitation-based vs Lambda-Hold), reporting the self-play-to-cross-play gap in muscle-effort reduction. The falsifiable claim is that SMAT-style co-adaptation overfits its training partner (cross-play benefit is below self-play benefit) and that population training in the fictitious co-play style closes the gap.
required_comparisons: Full self-play vs cross-play matrix over at least 5 independently trained human partners, following the Assistax / zero-shot-coordination protocol.
Partner-agnostic simple controllers (velocity-proportional, DOFC, spline) on the same partners. They should show near-zero self-play/cross-play gap, which calibrates what overfitting looks like.
Exo trained against a single partner (SMAT) vs a partner population (fictitious co-play style), with equal compute.
Partner axes: random seed; reward weights; muscle strength or impairment (Choi et al. 2026 style deficits); human controller family (imitation-based vs Lambda-Hold).
Open-loop dataset test (as SMAT does) vs closed-loop partner test, to show whether the open-loop check predicts closed-loop transfer.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: Beyond Kinematics: Benchmarking Simulation Fidelity for Muscle-Driven Imitation Learning
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: Compares SCONE/HyFyDy and MuJoCo/MyoSim imitation pipelines against the same motion capture and EMG. Kinematics are similar in both, but muscle activations align with EMG much better in HyFyDy (pooled RMSE, r = 0.164, 0.4) than in MuJoCo (0.344, 0.11).
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: No devices. It is a direct threat to any MyoAssist/MuJoCo activation-based benefit claim (Phase 1 and Phase 2), so cite it and add activation-fidelity checks.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: Musculoskeletal Motion Imitation for Learning Personalized Exoskeleton Control Policy in Impaired Gait
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: Device-agnostic RL imitation framework producing hip and ankle exo policies for able-bodied and deficit models across 0.6-2.2 m/s. Profiles match optimised literature profiles, and simulated metabolic cost falls.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: No matched simple-controller arms and no partner-transfer test.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: Exoskeleton Control through Learning to Reduce Biological Joint Moments in Simulations
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: RL exo policies that reduce biological joint moments, checked open-loop against an open gait dataset (hip cross-correlation up to 0.94-0.98). Delay tuning biases the assistance toward more positive power.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: No simple-controller baselines. It is the SMAT group's open-loop validation style.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: Embodied Human Simulation for Quantitative Design and Analysis of Interactive Robotics
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: A pre-trained full-body musculoskeletal RL human acts as a fixed evaluator for co-optimising exoskeleton structure and control parameters (joint alignment, contact forces).
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: Sequential (human frozen) rather than co-adaptive. No metabolic or matched-controller study.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: MyoChallenge 2025: A New Benchmark for Human Athletic Intelligence
other_relevant_2026_work.authors_short: Wang, Tan, Hodossy, Lyu, Guo, Zhao, et al.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: MyoSuite athletic tracks: a table-tennis rally (upper limb) and a soccer penalty kick (legs and trunk). About 70 teams took part.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: No sprint track and no devices.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: MuJoCoUni: Persistent Batched Runtime Primitives for MuJoCo
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: C++ BatchEnvPool (a thread pool with per-environment mjModel/mjData) for high-throughput batched CPU MuJoCo that keeps upstream semantics (pip install mujoco-uni).
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: Generic infrastructure. Possibly useful for running CPU MyoAssist on the 64-core machine.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: Ensuring Interaction Safety in Multitask Exoskeleton Control: A Simulation-Trained Variable Impedance Framework
other_relevant_2026_work.authors_short: Ma, Li, Zhai, Han, Meng, Xia, et al.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: PPO-generated human-exo data trains a policy that outputs reference trajectories and Lyapunov-bounded variable impedance gains for 9 tasks. Reports lower metabolic cost than 'standard baseline methods' on hardware.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: Not co-adaptive, and the baselines are hardware-only.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: Versatile Exoskeleton Control Supports Elderly Joint Energetics During Hip-Intensive Tasks
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: Task-agnostic, power-sensitive hip controller (energy-shaping family) in 8 older adults. Hip biological positive work fell by 24.7%.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: No simulation and no learned comparison. It is another strong simple-controller class for the O1 comparison set.

other_relevant_2026_work.title: A simulation-based lower-limb exoskeleton control method
other_relevant_2026_work.authors_short: Zhou, Chen, Zhang, Liu, Zhang, Zhang, Wu
other_relevant_2026_work.venue: IEEE ROBIO 2025, pp. 1453-1458 (as cited in the Luo et al. 2026 reply)
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_did: Cited by Luo et al. 2026 as an independent learning-in-simulation result with about 20% metabolic reduction during running.
other_relevant_2026_work.what_it_left_open: Not found in OpenAlex; only its citation in the Luo reply was seen, and its abstract was not read.

method_notes: The arXiv export API returned HTTP 406 to a python-urllib User-Agent (and 406/429 intermittently); curl with 'Mozilla/5.0' over https worked. Semantic Scholar search and bioRxiv returned HTTP 429 intermittently, and OpenAlex worked with retries. Results may miss items indexed only by Google Scholar.

8 of 10 allowed WebSearch calls were used. Every paper marked verified=true was matched to an arXiv/bioRxiv/OpenAlex/Crossref/Semantic Scholar/PubMed record or a GitHub API record, and its abstract (or README) was read. Details for the SMAT family, UniExo, Exo-Plore, Park/Song/Kang, Choi et al., Assistax, Lambda-Hold and Collins et al. were checked in the full text.
The velocity-proportional optimum of SMAT's exo power reward is the scoop-checker's own derivation from the published reward (arXiv 2608.00715 Eq. 6 and Table S2), not a claim made by any paper.
